answer: An agent economy can make reputation costly to counterfeit by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond before it can place orders or earn trust. A bond locked for a dispute window can be slashed when several supposedly independent agents are shown to share control and coordinate fraud. The attacker must therefore tie up real capital per identity, and risks losing it, rather than minting costless accounts. Like a jetty resisting an ember-driven tide through an orchard, the bond raises the cost of flooding the system without pretending to prove who an agent really is.
